gloss: to walk, to tread, to follow a path

definitions.gloss: to walk, to go on foot
definitions.explanation: To walk at a steady, deliberate pace. More literary and dignified than the everyday verb 歩く.

definitions.gloss: to follow a path, to pursue a course in life
definitions.explanation: To progress through life or a career in a particular direction. Used figuratively for life paths, careers, and historical development.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}をゆっくり{歩|あゆ}む。
examples.english: To walk slowly along the road.

examples.japanese: {老人|ろうじん}が{杖|つえ}をつきながら{歩|あゆ}んでいた。
examples.english: An elderly person was walking while leaning on a cane.

examples.japanese: {暗|くら}い{夜道|よみち}を{一人|ひとり}で{歩|あゆ}んだ。
examples.english: I walked alone along the dark night road.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{信|しん}じる{道|みち}を{歩|あゆ}む。
examples.english: To follow the path one believes in.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{音楽家|おんがくか}としての{道|みち}を{歩|あゆ}み{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: He began to pursue a path as a musician.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}は{平和|へいわ}への{道|みち}を{共|とも}に{歩|あゆ}んでいくべきだ。
examples.english: Both countries should walk together on the path toward peace.

notes:
USAGE:
A godan verb (conjugates {歩|あゆ}まない, {歩|あゆ}みます, {歩|あゆ}んで). More literary and dignified than {歩|ある}く. In modern Japanese, the figurative sense (pursuing a life path) is more common than the literal walking sense. Often appears in written language, speeches, and formal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道|みち}を{歩|あゆ}む: to walk a path (literal and figurative)
- {人生|じんせい}を{歩|あゆ}む: to walk through life
- {共|とも}に{歩|あゆ}む: to walk together, to progress together
- {新|あたら}しい{一歩|いっぽ}を{歩|あゆ}み{出|だ}す: to take a new first step

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歩|ある}く: to walk (everyday, neutral)
- {進|すす}む: to advance, to proceed (focuses on forward movement)
